summary: This informational RFC registers the media type used by the Content Delivery Network Interconnection protocol suite. It explains the registration process and how to use the required payload-type parameter, which says what kind of CDNI data an object contains.

plainLanguage.summary: CDNI uses one media type to label several kinds of messages exchanged between content delivery networks. A required parameter tells the receiver what kind of payload the message contains.

questions: what is the cdni ptype parameter
how do i register a cdni payload type
what does the cdni ptype parameter do
subtitle: A shared media type and registry for identifying CDNI message payloads.

tldr.problem: CDNI interfaces carry different kinds of data, and registering a separate media type for every payload would require many registrations.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers application/cdni with a required ptype parameter and establishes a registry of valid payload-type values.
tldr.outcome: New payload types require a specification and designated-expert review to support interoperable parsing.

today: RFC 7736 is an Informational document published in December 2015. The batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: One Media Type for CDNI Payloads
sections.content:
Content Delivery Network Interconnection (CDNI) defines interfaces for interconnected content delivery networks. Those interfaces transfer different payloads, many encoded in JSON. This RFC defines one media type to identify CDNI messages without registering a separate type for each payload.

The payload type can also be used as a reference in other CDNI data. A CDNI protocol specification can define a payload type, its encoding, and how a receiver parses it.
sections.plainLanguage: CDNI messages can carry different kinds of information. One shared media type identifies them, while a parameter specifies the particular payload type.

sections.title: The application/cdni Media Type
sections.content:
The registered type is application/cdni. Its required ptype parameter identifies the kind of CDNI message payload and must use a value from the CDNI Payload Types registry. The registration defines no optional parameters.

The media type is intended only for CDNI protocol exchanges. The RFC describes its use for sharing configuration and logging information and for content management and redirection requests. The payload encoding may be 8-bit or binary; generic logging information may be 7-bit or binary.
sections.plainLanguage: A CDNI message uses the label application/cdni and must include ptype. That parameter tells the receiver which registered payload format to parse.

sections.title: Registering Payload Types
sections.content:
IANA created the CDNI Payload Types subregistry to list valid values for ptype. A value is a visible ASCII string that excludes an equal sign, a double quote, and a semicolon, and it cannot exceed 256 characters.

Registration uses Specification Required review. A designated expert checks that a proposed value has a clear purpose, relates to a CDNI interface, does not duplicate existing functionality without justification, and gives enough encoding detail for interoperable parsers. The RFC says the registry was initially empty.
sections.plainLanguage: A new payload type needs a written specification and expert review. The review checks that the type is distinct, useful to a CDNI interface, and described well enough for different systems to parse it.

sections.title: Validation and Security
sections.content:
A generic media type does not explain how to interpret every possible payload. A receiver must understand the ptype value and the encoding associated with it. A non-CDNI or non-compliant implementation may misinterpret encoded data.

The RFC also warns that large logging payloads can overload clients and that failures to validate payloads can allow data extrusion. The individual CDNI interface specifications define their authentication, authorization, confidentiality, integrity, and privacy requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver must check the payload type and parse the data using its specified format. Large or incorrectly interpreted payloads can create security or resource problems.
